title: Bringing Continual Learning into Enterprises — Samuel Denton, Applied Compute
talk_summary: Samuel Denton of Applied Compute describes a 2x2 taxonomy of distillation along offline/online traces and offline/online hints, showing that targeted behavioral changes (turn-limit wrapping, hyperlink formatting) can be trained into models without degrading base task performance. The core techniques are per-step hint injection and LLM-judge token masking, but they require model weight training, not prompt-level orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Per-step hint injection instead of upfront instructions
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than putting a behavioral instruction at the start of a rollout, they use a judge to decide where in the trajectory to inject the hint, then teach only the next few steps after that point.
takeaways.evidence_quote: rather than injecting a hint to the beginning of a rollout, we use a judge to essentially decide where in the rollout we should be injecting hints
takeaways.numbers: KL learning signal decreases as distance from hint grows

takeaways.what_they_do: An LLM judge samples which tokens/steps of the teacher signal are actually relevant to the target behavior, filtering out irrelevant stylistic preferences that cause catastrophic degradation.
takeaways.numbers: improved learning of out-of-distribution behavior while avoiding catastrophic degradation

takeaways.technique: Separate behavior-adherence metric from task-success metric
takeaways.what_they_do: They track task-complete-call rate (did the agent exhibit the target behavior) separately from test pass rate (did the underlying task still succeed), and report the intersection as the real pass rate.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the goal is we want to raise the SWE-bench pass rate performance while not degrading the test pass rate
takeaways.numbers: task-complete call rate 22% -> 60% with test pass rate roughly constant

takeaways.technique: Targeted single-behavior hints with explicit wrap-up cues
takeaways.what_they_do: They craft a concrete hint telling the agent it is near its turn limit and must finalize and verify before calling the submit tool, targeting one specific behavior at a time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You are near your 40-turn limit. There's only about three turns left... finalize and verify your fix and then call this tool
takeaways.numbers: task-complete call rate rose from ~22% to ~60%
